This is a tactical game in the vein of Commandos: Behind Enemy Lines, Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood, Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, etc. Basically, if you like the highly tactical squad-based tactical RPGs, this is a game for you.

Setting-wise, this one puts you in the shoes of the Soviet partisans deep behind the enemy lines in the nazi-occupied part of the Soviet union in 1941. A historical no-brainer for a game of this kind. As a result, there's no need to stretch the story at all and the sequence of missions is rather natural. Seeing as some reviewers here mention poor scripting and voice acting, it must be said that the Russian version is fairly decent, but very difficult to translate into what is today thought of as colloquial English, while still sounding genuine and historically and culturally appropriate.

There are 15 missions that tend to get progressively more difficult as you progress (but not punishingly so) and the stealth approach is just as satisfactory as a gung-ho approach (also a very valid option, unlike with some other games of the genre).

Just finished the game and it was quiet interesting experience. If you like Commandos, Desperados, etc.. you should buy it and give it a try.
I believe that if devs release another game and fix the mentioned issues it could easily be a 9 or a 10.

Pros:
- Interesting setting and story
- Variety of maps and objectives
- Camp system (build buildings, go to missions for certain resources,etc..)
- Hero system (skills, upgrades,etc..) - you also get to select which ones to bring into battle
- Inventory system which allows you to equip whatever you want to suit your gameplay
- More action than similar games (maybe that's not positive depending on point of view)

Cons
- Various small annoying issues/bugs that could have been easily fixed with some QoL fixes
- Inventory system has some really annoying issues and the whole "extra" stuff you find it makes game really annoying to manage at times
- Camp system although it's a nice addition compared to others, I think it could have bee really great. After you build the basic buildings there's really not much else you can do
- Weapon upgrading ; again a nice system but could have been easily improved to be even more great and offer more customizations
- Skill system; again a nice addition but many skills are similar to others 
- Moral mechanism; seemed like a nice idea but you tend to forget as you progress the game. Maybe if it could have been more complex e.g. with consequences on missions it would have been better.
- You can select 3 heroes in each missions (with some exceptions) which imo is really bad, cause certain characters are left unplayed
- Last mission (wayyy too easy and small for final one) -> also it's final mission you should have been able to select the whole squad!
It is hard to evaluate this game in a Yes/No basis. This game looks a better version of Shadow Tactics, but it looks unfinished in some ways. It is also short.

Even if you are fan of the tactics genre, you may be disappointed with Partisans 1941. The mission quality is a mixed bag as they are not fully fixed to specific characters, rather than being crafted around their respective abilities (which you may not even fully unlock by the end). This means that the missions are open to more generic tactics gameplay, leading to a sense of repetition. Further to this, you can take characters on a mission only to realize afterwards they were a poor choice for the circumstances.

Outside of the missions there is a basic partisan camp management system, which allows for a bit of a breather and character interactions to progress the story. While I like the idea, the system is only surface level, slowing down the experience as you collect and sort food and supplies. There is also a moral mechanic, but I completely forgot about it early on (as long as you do the available moral tasks and don't steal from the locals, you'll encounter virtually zero challenge with the mechanic).

Overall I did enjoy my time with Partisans, but is does have numerous shortcoming which hinder the experience. Under-baked mechanics, AI bugs, UI usability issues, and general lack of polish make it hard to recommend over alternatives like Blades of the Shogun or Desperados III. Worth a try if you're itching for more tactics gameplay, just know that others have done it better.

Great game I really enjoyed it. I'm a big fan of real time tactic games and I've played all the games I could find in this genre. If you're a fan of commandos, definitely try this one, gives you the same feeling but with a much greater look. The gameplay overall is great except for the times that there are several possible commands in a close range on the screen. For instance if you want to take cover and there is dead body just beside the cover point, you would have hard time to find a position of the camera and the mouse pointer that would allow you to do that. I had encountered similar other situations several times during the game. Other than that, everything was perfect and enjoyable.

The skill tree idea for each character was also good, gave you effective options on how you like to play with your hero. There are 8 characters that are fairly different in their unique abilities (each hero has 2) but other than that the other abilities in their skill tree were shared with other characters. Not everyone had the same side skills, but you could find each of the skills being shared with 3 or more characters. Which was ok because you could have the same skill set for a hero with a more useful unique skills.

As for the characters themselves, in most missions I found myself that I only needed 2 heroes and other ones were mostly just a carry bag to loot food and materials. And those 2 were the same ones during the first half of the game before a new character was unlocked that replaced one of the previous 2 until the end of the game and during all DLC missions. The reason was of course that I like to take the stealth approach and those specific characters were great for my play style. Also the option that the game allows you to pick the characters you want for each mission (except for the main character being forced to pick for most of the missions) was good but because of that during the whole game I barely used the characters other than the ones I liked.

There's a camp in this game which is where you spend your time between the missions. The idea is very similar to what a 2002 game (Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood) had, and I didn't see any specific improvement on that idea, except for not having to actually play the random resource collection missions in this game. It's great that they have used the idea, but for a 2020 game I hoped they had added more to it.

The resource collection and base building aspect of the game was just OK, at the very first encounter it sounded promising but very soon it became just something to do between missions with very few options. During the main missions you can collect lots of different stuff from an empty bottle to gun parts, medical resources, and ... At first you might think each would be useful to make something specific that might help you later in some way. Something like a unique weapon or upgrade. But there is no such thing. All the stuff you collect are either food, or construction materials. Food gets consumed by the characters daily, and the materials, no matter what they were can be used for upgrades in the camp or do side missions when staying in the camp. I was quite disappointed by the whole "resource collection and base building" element of the game. It could be amazing, but it has turned out quite simple.

What I said above are just some improvements that could make this game even much better that it already is. Overall I definitely recommend this game. The gameplay is great, the missions are very well designed and in some cases push you to try strategies that you might never use. In my case I always avoid conflictions and try to do things silently, but there are some missions that there are no such options available or at least it is much easier to just make a blood bath. Or as another example I normally like to wipe out of the whole map from any enemies, but for the missions in mission mode in the 5-star difficulty, you almost have no other options to take a speed-run approach, trying to avoid any unnecessary act and killing as few as possible. I would never do that if I wasn't forced to by the game, and it felt great when I did it. It made the missions much much shorter and I was feeling I hadn't experienced the mission enough, but it felt great just to do the task so quickly and so neatly.

As a big fan of Action Puzzle games, as I call them (Commandos, Desperados, etc.), I was quite excited about Partisans 1941. It seemed like the devs wanted to try a different approach to the genre, but after 100% the game I'm not sure that any of the core changes worked out well.

TL;DR. The game is really unpolished with dozens of small issues of all kinds popping up here and there. Also, the game provides no real challenge (I’d say no challenge at all) or incentive to combine the skill of partisans to achieve the mission goals. Instead of several distinguishable characters with distinguishable abilities, we have 8 semi-Jacks of all Trades, only three of which can be taken on a single mission at once. I can still recommend the game, but only if you haven’t played other similar games (especially the modern ones like Shadow Tactics or Desperados III). Otherwise you will most likely find the Partisans 1941 experience subpar.

The game is thematically very close to Commandos series — same theme (war vs Nazis), similar objectives (kill leaders, destroy a huge artillery gun, etc.), no complex storyline (just go kill this or destroy this), etc. The game tried to move away from a time-proven formula by introducing new mechanics, but I personally think that none of them worked out great.

- Looter shooter system. There are guns of different types and different qualities. Ammo, throwables, mines, medkits — everything is an inventory item now and must be looted instead of being usable skills. Therefore, each character has a limited amount of space. To my mind it added nothing of value to the genre other than a need to sort the inventory mess after sorting another mess while trying to pick items using an awkward and sometimes glitching UI. You can’t actually go permanent gunz blazing, so all that system seems to be applicable only under specific circumstances that are somewhat rare.

- Intermission camp. Instead of playing one mission after another, we now have a camp where all partisans sit around the bonfire and attempt Global Map tasks. There are Food and Materials resources which can be gathered during missions by looting dead enemies or various objects and then spending time sorting the inventory mess. Food is spent to feed your party. Materials can be used to construct various buildings that provide access to makeshift consumables, weapon upgrades, healing as well as additional sources of Food income. Again, I’m not sure what value this adds to the game – I’ve completed the campaign on Normal difficulty and I never ever had a situation when I needed any of the buildings except for the Food ones. And I only needed those, because out of eight people you can only take three on the main missions while others are just sitting there eating the food reserves and participating in secondary tasks that grant experience points.

- Skill Trees. Instead of a predetermined set of usable skills each character has a predetermined Skill Tree which can not be reset! As you gain experience (there is a certain incentive to kill every enemy on every map) you can move down the Skill Tree to unlock 1-2 usable skills and some passive ones (running speed, body carrying speed, melee / grenades / weapons proficiency, more inventory space, etc). And again, I don’t see any benefits here — passive skills are often duplicated between characters and even usable skills are somewhat similar (AOE damage in a circle or AOE damage in a cone, pacify with a slingshot or pacify with chloroform, etc). So instead of a shorter roster of distinctive specialists with distinctive skills and personalities, we have almost a dozen similar 3D models with different voices.

As far as other aspects of the game are concerned, they remained pretty much the same. But, man, this game is EXTREMELY unpolished. Small issues of all kinds are literally everywhere! Review limitations won't allow to mention everything that I encountered, but here are some:

Sometimes the partisans won’t complete an action, especially if you order them to place a mine — they simply stand still with the mine outline being visible.

The cones of enemy sight are really unprecise at times and they might detect you outside the visual color zone. On top of that, some of the in-game objects seem to be blocking the cones, but the enemies can still see and even walk through them (especially noticeable with truck cabins). By the way, a very useful mechanic of placing a mark on the ground to detect enemies that can see the mark is not available in the game at all.

There were multiple UI issues throughout the game: more than dozen of times I wasn’t able to loot dead enemies until I rotated the camera under a very specific angle. Inventory sometimes vanished and I needed to close the inventory window and open it again. Some of the Global Map secondary tasks always showed twice in the completion window although clearly only one was completed. There is a tooltip missing for the amount of Materials you will get from a Global Map task.

Several mission-related examples: there is a brief cutscene introducing the prison guy, where he uses a [strike]Tanuki[/strike] whistle to lure an enemy into the bushes and then perform a knife kill in the face with the special skill. Well, guess what? You can’t do this sequence in the actual game! Because every such attempt will result in an immediate red exclamation mark and alarm — you can only use a knife in the face skill from behind which is pretty much useless in most cases. At the same mission Zorin explains that blowing up AA Guns is a loud undertaking, so we need to destroy the Comm Center first. This is clearly not the case, because I’ve blown up the guns before going to the Comm Center and nothing happened — nobody sounded an alarm or anything.

Or take the AOE skills of any of the four partisans who have them (the sports guy, the tough lady, the grandpa and the one-eyed commissar) — their efficiency is very questionable, because partisans can be easily wounded or killed while using these skills! It does add to the realism of the situation, but this realism takes away any practical uses (in other similar games all AOE targets die at once).

Inventory auto-sort function is awkward to say the least. It can’t automatically sort items of different shapes (you have 4 empty spaces in a straight line, but found an item with 4 spaces as a square? Sorry, please sort the inventory manually). It also can’t sort identical items close to each other, which is a real pain in arse at the Intermission camp warehouse.

Another thing that I didn’t like personally — the game provides no challenge. As I’ve mentioned a bit earlier, 80% of my playtime was controlling Zorin, the very first playable character available in the game, to eliminate everything and everyone with a knife. There is no incentive to use your characters skills in combination in order to overcome a difficult situation, because there are no difficult situations to begin with (I was playing on Partisan difficulty). Back to Battle DLC introduced those one-time missions and with all modifiers turned on, the maps became quite challenging, but unnecessary annoying because of how enemy reinforcements work.

Why do I still recommend the game in the end? Two main reasons:

Fantastic concept that is frequently stepped on by janky and non-intuitive controls. On the tin, this very nearly delivers what you would want in a game like this: interesting character mechanics, thoughtful voice acting, and solid variety of missions in the progression. 

However, even with the whole slow-time focus mechanic, it's really agony trying to control your partisans in any situation requiring precise maneuvering. Some objects have to be clicked directly, while others you have to frantically click around to find the hitbox of a weird and imprecise feeling pop-out menu. Extremely inconsistent, which makes it annoying to master.

On the battle maps, the inflexibility of the camera makes it challenging to comfortably maneuver. You have the benefit of full 360 degree rotation, but no tilt control hardly any zoom. It's such a small margin of zoom that it nearly makes it pointless to include. But I feel like the main issue is that there is no intelligent cutaway system (a la Sims), and any object that disrupts the camera/cursor will likewise block your clicked selection. Especially frustrating when trying to make small, tactical adjustments when things start getting bonkers.

This general jank continues through the characters, levels, as well as in the over-world camp system. I loved the idea of getting stuff during missions that would carry over to camp supply, and those supplies can be buttressed by doing asynchronous, over-world missions. But again, the whole thing is diminished by the inconvenient means of exchanging gear between characters (handled chiefly through another bizarre pop out menu when click and drag is not available). 

On the first several missions, I missed the opportunity to send various squadmembers on the async missions, thinking I had selected them for tasks, but when viewing another task for a different partisan, it deselected the original (unless "applied" via a second button click).

The inventory menu system is pretty wacky as well, and besides the aforementioned item exchange difficulty, good decisions were made into weird results. For instance, they had the good sense to put 'store all' and 'auto sort' buttons on the party members. Makes it easy to  dump stuff post mission, since clicking things is a nightmare here. But even with the forethought of the clickable categories, the filtering system doesn't behave like you'd expect; items get grouped separately from other like items. Ammunition of the same type ends up on different rows. There are reasons for some of it (eg. item quality for guns), but for most others it doesn't feel intuitive at all.

I really wanted to focus this review on specific, control-based aspects, but I also feel like because of the above concerns, it makes some gameplay quality fumbles feel less excusable. At the end of the day, it's a weak stealth mechanic. Most patrols on static, pre-defined routes. Same old stealth rpg tropes of an arrow sticking out of a guy's face, but as long as your timer elapses: "huh, must've been the wind" before going back to the same spot.

This part specifically deals with the English version of the game: lack of a large enough pool of contextual dialogue, and just generally lazy writing that diminishes the seriousness of the occupation motif. I'm sure there is a lot lost in translation here, some breakdown between Daedalic, Alter, and the subbed version we ended up with. Because the ambient npc dialogue, constant "my eyes hurt from crying" from every NPC, and even the sort of superficial overworld campfire conversations, all sort of felt like big Mass Effect: Andromeda, "my face is tired" level of banality.

I took this many characters of your bandwidth here because I ultimately like the game. It's entertaining, but immensely frustrating because of these oversights and limitations. In some good ways, it feels like playing a tiny Company of Heroes on the Foxhole engine. In nearly every bad way, it feels like playing a tiny Company of Heroes on the Foxhole engine.

[h1]RECOMMENDATION: Buy on sale[/h1]

Partisans 1941 at its best is a fun, challenging tactics game in a unique setting, but at its worst is a buggy, frustrating stealth game where the lack of polish outshines the game's pros. It's a game that doesn't quite realize its potential but still provides an entertaining experience. Unless you already know you like real-time tactics games, and really enjoy a WWII Eastern European setting, I'd wait to buy the game on sale, where it's definitely worth the price.

[b]Pros:[/b]
-Systematically wiping out squads of enemies or preparing a makeshift defense to hold off waves of enemies with only 3-4 characters or 'partisans' are very satisfying. Once you get the timing down, synchronizing your units' actions is rewarding.

-The game gives a decent amount of tools to take on missions, while also implementing an inventory management system that makes you prioritize what's worth picking up between in-mission items and food/supplies that help feed your partisans, improve your base, and create make-shift items and weapon upgrades. You won't be able to pick up everything you find. I normally don't enjoy inventory management but I think it enhanced the game in this case.

-Each partisan has customizable skills with their own strengths, deficiencies, and unique skills. Some units can more easily sneak around, some are better at stealthily eliminating enemies, and some units have special combat abilities for quickly wiping out squads. Partisans will have their shortcomings you can't change, so you'll want to assess which are best suited for stealthier versus combat-heavy missions. 

-As far as strategy games go, Partisans 1941 is relatively brief. I played on [u]Normal[/u] and it was my first time playing this genre of tactics game, and it took me about 18-22 hours. More experienced players, or anyone playing on easy, will probably have a quicker play-through.

-The voice-acting is immersive, none of which is in English. As a non-Russian speaker, I can't fully access the quality of the voice-acting, but it sounds authentic and believable, nothing ridiculous or over the top. It makes you feel like you're actually fighting on the Eastern Front.

-The gameplay mostly strikes the right balance between stealth and combat. Actively engaging in shootouts will quickly deplete your characters' limited ammo until last few missions, but the game isn't afraid to throw overwhelming numbers against you to force careful planning and quick reactions to survive engagements. 

-The characters have just enough of a personality to feel human, with a few short dialogues between missions, but don't expect to become majorly attached to them.

-There are a few opportunities for 'environmental' kills and events that spice-up missions. 

-The game does not whitewash the horrors of war inflicted upon civilians. The game won't show you anything especially graphic but you do feel the brutality of the occupation. While the plot is pretty barebones, theses moments provide decent story motivation for the player and characters (mostly).  

[b]Cons:[/b]
-It feels like this game needed much more play-testing before launch, particularly for finding bugs. Too often characters will accidentally (not) pick-up bodies, inadvertently leave cover, or aim at target well outside their weapon's range. Plenty of times you think you're moving a group of units into bushes (which conceal your units) only for one of them to be standing outside the bushes and give away your position. Some character's abilities are bugged and alert your enemies when ordinarily you'd think it wouldn't. Other times a unit will take a terrible route to a destination (I don't think you can set waypoints). 

-The worst implementation issue is when loading a quick-save during a mission (which new players will likely be doing a lot). Instead of reloading everything as it was, enemies will instead be at the beginning of their patrol route. I've even seen enemies seemingly come back to life off a quick-save, or already start on alert. You can mitigate this partially by quick-saving before starting a careful maneuver, but its still an inconvenience in a game where precision is critical. 

-The cover system is very haphazard. Objects you'd think would serve as cover, like walls near open doorways, aren't. This can make some of the battles inside buildings unintentionally difficult without liberal use of grenades.

-The fact I am experiencing these issues two years after the game's release means they aren't getting fixed. The player can learn to play around them, but proceed at your own peril.

-The music is completely forgettable to nonexistent. It's not a dealbreaker but a strong score would have given the latter missions, particularly the finale, a bigger emotional punch. 

-The story itself doesn't feel like it ever escalates. I mentioned liking the characters and mature themes, but the way the story's portrayed, the characters never meaningfully develop past their couple character traits. There's no emotional conflict between the characters or over the story's events, and despite the crimes perpetrated against the civilian population, it feels like your partisans respond almost flatly and matter-of-factly, which feels out-of-place when the game literally shows pits full of corpses and children wondering where their parents are. This feels like a big missed opportunity even if strategy games don't always emphasis story and atmosphere.

-The final mission, while a good test of the player's skill, ultimately falls flat. It's combat-centric and suffers the most from the half-implemented cover system, especially for indoor fights. The mission itself almost feels inconsequential. There's barely any build-up, no comments from the character's before or during the mission about how this is a turning point and decisive battle, and once the mission concludes the game just...ends. All you get is a letter with some game stills that says 'good job' and 'the Soviet people will always fight back'. Nothing about the German occupiers retreating, no in-game ramifications of your success, not even one-line character endings. The complete lack of a payoff makes the mission feel tacked on. The penultimate mission, which have well-established stakes from earlier missions, comes across as a more fitting end to the campaign. It's another aspect of the game that feels disappointing and underdeveloped.

The game is on sale for six USD at the time of writing. At that price, the entertainment value is excellent. But for anyone on a tight budget or thinking of buying the game at full price, I'd recommend looking elsewhere or waiting for a sale. The game's shortcomings don't diminish the joy I felt when a carefully planned mission goes off smoothly, but the underdeveloped gameplay elements, story, and music leaves much to be desired that I hope is addressed in a sequel.

There are several interesting new features, such as the morale impact on the characters and the various injuries that limit their abilities and forces the player to adapt to the situation.

There is also a light base resource management, similar to Robin Hood that had introduced it in the past, which is nice too, although I would prefer it a bit more challenging. Due to its easinness, a very good (and historically true) feature loses its potential. I am talking about the fact that sometimes you will discover food and resources that belong to the common folk and if you take them the team morale is decreased to reflect the negative impact. The problem is that, if you have even a minor reasonable management you will never face the dilemma seriously. But nevertheless, it's interesting as a feature.

The Hard mode is a lot of times exactly this -hard- as it permits no save at all, with the exception of only a couple autosaves in some missions. Putting aside the bugs that may force a frustrating restart, this mode trully succeeds in leading the players with different approaches into trying something new.
The stealthy, silent lover will have to inevitably shoot at some point and realize that he may be able to kill some enemies unnoticed but almost everytime will have to strategically place the other partisans in positions that in case of a screw up will defend their discovered comrade. And there will be screw ups surely!
On the other hand, the all guns blazing eastern rambo will have to keep an eye on the ammo, the inevitable injuries from the combat that will impact the ability of a partisan to even shoot sometimes and will appreciate the stealth approach a bit more.

There is an rpg element also as the characters level up and gain different abilities.
As it is impossible to fill the whole ability tree, the game this way gains replayability, again by letting the player to try new things.

Last but not least, the storyline is set on the eastern front and through the eyes of the people that fought the nazi there, which is way underpresented in both the game and movie industry despite the gigantic importance on the course of the war.

The bugs as mentioned before are present unfortunatelly, so some patience sometimes is needed. Apart from the occasional fps drops I think that none of them is gamebreaking but keep the game below a perfect score definetely.

I would recommend also, for people like me that speak no russian at all, to play the game in the russian language for voice and english text at least on the second playthrough or during the non campaign missions.

I want to love this game but there are too many flaws in the gameplay that make it really hard to play and not in a good way.
1. The detection system is bad. It is hypersensitive and enemies sometimes even see through walls. On other occasions they don't detect the characters at all, even when they're right in front of them. This makes stealth missions (of which there are a few) almost unplayable.
2. The ammo is highly limited, which can be a good thing if balanced otherwise but in most cases it's not even worth using guns at all and just rely on things like knife throwing or explosives which have a 100 % chance to hit and in the case for knifes are even unlimited and in the case of explosives are usually abundant.
3. The food system is not very well implemented and it takes a while to get used to as it's not explained properly. To get more food you can either just rely on the 1 x free food gathering per day or you can build a kitchen. If you build a kitchen, not only does it take time and resources but also you'll have to spend food to get food.
4. The pathfinding of your characters is atrocious. They'll rather run around three corners directly into enemy sight instead of the slightly longer way around enemies. That would be fine if the characters would be controlled more directly. But this way you have to rely on the terrible pathfinding.
4.5 Related to the pathfinding is that sometimes when you select more than one character to be in the same spot behind cover for example, one character will stay behind the cover while the other just runs to the other side. You can't be more precise because you can't really scroll in too much. 
5. Abilities are incredibly unbalanced. While most of them are quite cool ideas, they're not very well executed. The already mentioned knife throwing is a guaranteed one hit kill if you're close enough (and again you have to rely on the terrible pathfinding here) which is unlimited as long as you don't forget to pick up your knife (makes sense eh?). Well that logic applies to most ablities, you have a certain cooldown and you can use it afterwards again. BUT WAIT, without telling it in the skill description some of the ablities have limited use. This might not be too bad if it was limited use per mission and it would have to "recharge" again until you leave for the partisan camp but no, they're limited use per character until the end of the game. 3 uses of the same ability you didn't even know had a cooldown? Well you're out of luck now, can't use the ability anymore.
6. The "natural" boundaries in the maps not only feel incredibly unnatural and generally bad. The characters can perform all kinds of stunts but are completely incapable when they're supposed to go up the slightlest of slopes.
7. The AI is just weird and overpowered, no matter the difficulty really. I appreciate some challenge but I want it to feel fair which it doesn't here. The AI always exactly knows where you are when one character has been seen by anyone, even if the reporter is being killed before they can shoot. This also ties in with the problem that using guns to quickly take out enemies is essentially useless because, even when enemies are outside of hearing range, they still will know what happened. Additionally enemies often manage to onehit characters, even if the characters are in cover.
It's obvious that enemies aren't characters like the player characters and more random number generators, which I always dislike in games.

The game has a lot of potential but it is very much unpolished and I doubt it can be fixed, even if the devs wanted to. It's not like the game feels like a cashgrab, it definitely has potential and the setting is somewhat unique.

This game has its potentials, but unfortunately I think it's ruined by the pack of small issues everywhere in the game. Seems to be a beginner project where devs tried to create a fusion of Commandos 2 and XCOM, but failed to deliver to either of the audience.

[list]
[*] When saving, the game auto-screenshots for you, and pops up on the bottom right, which covers some UI buttons and is very annoying.
[*] Firefight is terrible. I don't like RNG based fight while some enemies have long health bars so they can tank some shots. I can't imagine people playing on highest (I played on normal) while managing to stay sane. You can apparently 100%-accurately throw a deadly knife, but you cannot aim an rifle even if it's within knife range. And apparently you can 100%-accurately shoot a dog, but not a soldier.
[*] Alert system together with the firefight is not fun. So you give me rifles, and you give me explosives, and when I started firefight (in mission "Hunter" at the very beginning), it seemed that the whole map reinforced. Apparently you can shout farther than rifle can shoot accurately.
[*] Alert-related missions and achievements suck. I don't mind going stealth - this is my style - but with all those bs it's not very enjoyable. My patience only lasted until I missed one of those achievements while going completely stealth in mission "First Aid".
[*] The control is a bit clunky. I do like waypoints which Commandos, Desperado, and Shadow Tactics do not have, but overall the characters are much less responsive compared to the RTT mentioned.
[*] The game tries to integrate too many functionality into mouse clicks only- pick up knifes, pick up corpses, shelter in cover, pick up loots, shoot, and this causes lots of minor problems like you will find it hard to pick up something near a cover, you are sometimes not able to pick up your knifes (as Zorin), etc.
[*] You can't double click when choosing to use an utility - you must single click it otherwise your second click will cancel the usage.
[*] You can't highlight enemies (Alt) when choosing to use an utility or skill - if cancels the usage and you will be surprised that you shoot the rifle instead of throwing a knife.
[*] High rank officer GPS-locating lower rank officers. It seems that high rank officer (titled an Golden Eagle) will randomly try to chat with lower rank officers, and if you happen to have killed one, it might start a search (which will invalidate some of the "without being found" achievements, I think, that seems to be how I missed the achievement during "First Aid" as I stealth-killed everyone), or the high rank officer might walk straight to the corpse wherever you hide it. STUPID. STUPID. VERY STUPID. I simply lost my patience after this.
[*] Some of the camp projects are just better than others, what's the point of those inferior ones? Just wasting my resources that can be used to improve the RNG?
[*] Skill tree requires you to put exactly 3 points in every row to unlock the next row; problem is, some of the perks have pre-requisites in previous rows, which forces you to pick up some unwanted useless skills if you want to advance to the final row.
[/list]

There are many minor issues like those, and are really damaging the gameplay. If you don't mind all kinds of stupid bugs, and like XCOM-like RNG-based firefights, you might want to try this when there is a discount.

A decent enough Commandos-like if that's what you're looking for.

Be aware that this is much closer to the original Commandos than it is to games like Shadow Tactics, that have done huge work to refine the formula in terms of systems, UI design and enemy AI. If you've played some of those more modern games, you may have been spoiled and could find it difficulty to go back to something like Partisans, which is rather rough around the edges.

The base management layer of the game is barely worth mentioning. It scarcely affects anything and quickly becomes an unnecessary exercise in clicking just to get to the next mission.

The biggest shortcomings to be aware of are the UI and the enemy AI. On the UI front, controls are fiddly, and the outcome of your actions is often unclear. Sometimes you'll be detected for unknown reasons, and the game does little to show you things like sound raidus *before* you take an action. That means there's lots of trial and error involved.

The enemy AI is just straight up bad. On finding an enemy corpse, sometimes they'll telepathically know exactly where all your partisans are, others they'll just stand there like idiots until the alert timer runs down. They also straight up can't handle indoor environments, regularly getting stuck in doorways, but thankfully most of the game takes place outside. This dodgy AI also makes the forced stealth sections a chore.

The really interesting twist here is that, unlike most games in the genre, combat is actually a viable option. When things get loud, the game actually handles tactical, cover-based combat pretty well. It just adds  a bit of welcome variety to proceedings.

All in, killing your way through maps full of Nazis is as satisfying as it's ever been, bugs and shonky AI aside.

This game gets worse the more you play it. 
There are characters that get stuck in bushes after cutscenes. Items that can't be pick up after being placed. Characters falling in the water and getting stuck in the water. You have bandages that you can't use sometimes too for no reason, even though you want to heal your almost dead partisans.

The enemy knows exactly where you are if put them on red alert, even if you are far, far away from them and hiding. They literally run you down no matter where you go or may be hiding. This means throwing a grenade and then running to a hiding spot, unseen the whole time, while your whole team is no where near the scene, also hiding, is not a valid option; they'll all get outnumbered in seconds by every soldier on the map and killed instantly that way. In other words, guerilla warfare is not something you can do in this game, even though these partisans seem willing and equipped to do that in this game. It's either full stealth or epic firefight.

There's inconsistencies in the gameplay. Sometimes your character will go for the stealth kill no problem. Other times they get really close to the enemy and start shooting, get into melee combat instead or stand there, both ways sounding the alarm. Same with enemy vision. Some enemies don't see you in their cone and you know its safe. Other times they 'see you' and sound the alarm, even though the enemy cones clearly don't see your character. 

Things are also unclear. At the camp, the missions have a supply icon of 50. I have 30 supplies and want more supplies. I go on the mission. The next day I neither earn nor lose supplies, even though I succeeded in the mission. Why is that supply Icon of 50 there if I neither lose nor gain 50 supplies by completing it? Missions you play are also unclear. In the tank mission, the captain doesn't mention that we need a bomb, or that we need to find one, meaning you're going to spend a lot of time confused and roaming the map wondering how and where you get a bomb for the tank. Same with the mission with the blonde partisan woman where you have to find the village chief. You find him, you get in his face, you're there again confused for a while not knowing that you have to kill the all the enemies here and there around him to interact with him. The player still has to figure out what you need to do in the mission even though there are mission objectives written out. 

Basic features that you may have seen in other games like Desperados 3 or Shadow Tactics are also missing here. The radius of how much noise your weapons make are unknown to you, meaning you have to guess and test yourself if others will hear your guns, knives and explosions. The camera also gives you the choice to either have the ability to rotate the camera with Q E or to move the camera up-down-left-right with the mouse. You can't pick both, but the game would be smoother with both. It's yes or no one or the other. 

Characters that get shot next to or on top of another body will pretty much die because the revive button is the same as the pick up button, the loot button and the cover button. So once the enemies that shot him go away and you get to him, the guy is going to do die before you can pick up all the bodies around him and put them somewhere else. This is the mechanic that will piss you off the most and drive you away from the game out all these issues.

All of this along with playing it on hard mode, which gives you zero saves for usually hour long missions and you have a progressively frustrating and raging experience. You're going to spend hours and days on single missions since it's already natural to mess up on top of all these issues hindering you. You have to do the missions over and over until you get it down perfect, with no characters stuck in place bugs, no pointless deaths because you can't click on your dying teammate, and more (There are still more bugs and problems I didn't mention on top of what I already listed).

The game is still fun, being able to customize character equipment, immersing yourself in a chill, stealth experience thanks to the music and style, being on edge which bullet will hit who during the occasional firefight, and simple management at your base. Unfortunately, I would not recommend this game to others to experience this rage inducing jank. In fact, as much as I like this game and genre and want to complete a single playthrough, my interest is dying because of the above issues cockblocking the completion of my endless attempts playing the same missions (the big betty mission especially). After dozens of hours, days in a row playing through the same mission then having to start over just because of something like a body on my partisan being in the way reviving him in time, just because he got caught at the end of the mission picking up a body. Your temper will explode too when this happens to you. Game's been out for about two years too from this review, so I would assume most if not all of these issues should have been fixed by now. Find a different game or heed my warning please.

Why?

If you enjoyed playing Commandos back in the day, then this is the closest thing you're going to see to a fully modernised sequel.

This is the 3rd game in the same genre from Daedalic after Shadow Tactics - Blades of the Shogun and Desperados III. If you enjoyed either of those then you're going to enjoy this.

For me this is the best real-time tactics game Daedalic have released so far. It goes further than their previous titles by adding in a home base where you can build up your camp, make food, modify weapons and go on interim missions to gain resources for crafting. Now this aspect of the game isn't very developed as yet and is a bit simplistic, but it adds a new dimension to the genre and gives the campaign missions a feeling of continuity as the resources and weapons that you scrounge during a mission can be taken back to base and shared among your group of partisans.

The graphics are excellent, although I'd like the zoom to be able to zoom in a little closer.

Controls are pretty good, though as usual with these games the characters don't always do eaxctly what you tell them and they sometimes go loud when you don't intend them to. However in Easy and Normal modes you can save and load at any time and the save/load times are very quick so it's easy to re-load a save if it all goes pear shaped.

I'm not a big fan of story based games, but the story in this one is pretty good. Historical accuracy is also good.

This is one of those games where I felt trult saddened when it ended, that I will miss the game characters now that the war is over and it'd be great to see a sequel to this.

Any negative reviews that tell you "just play Shadow Tactics" or "just play Desperados III" - ignore them. Play all three!

Oh yeah, and enemies are really really bad at using doors.

Overall its an enjoyable game - if a little tedious at times, and if you like the genre definitely worth playing. 6.5/10.

It does Russian history justice for a change. Won't fit certain narrative, though, but that's what CoH2 is for.

As an X-COM and Silent Storm fan, I got really excited about this game.
While it looks like a cool strategy at first glance, it actually gets very repetitive after a while.
All the missions are like:
- scout the map, walk through bushes that make you invisible
- set up a perfect ambush by surrounding a group of enemies
- die immediately and try again if you messed the previous up
- repeat for how many enemy patrols/guards there are on the map
- collect 27 bullets, one gun and a can of beans from 8 corpses
Scouting, killing single enemies one by one, preparing ambushes and quick saving/loading is like 97% of the time, the rest is actual firefights that happen so quick you barely manage to command your troops to throw a grenade.

This is a strategy game similar to the old Commandos but without the deep strategy and gimmicks. As almost every Daedalic Game it has a lot of things but lacks of depth. It's not a flaw it's just like they do everything. 
Game has a good story, solid mechanics (even if they are a bit repetitive).
Now why the negative review? 
There are two major issues which made the game unplayable and unfun, unless you savescum a lot.
First, and this is a VERY stupid issue, putting common \ powerful \ elite enemies in a realistic strategic game is dumb as hell, almost as dumb as "weapon rarity", which is in game but whatever.
A bullet is a bullet, doesn't matter if you are a common grunt or the general of the SS. This is WW2 not modern warfare, if I shoot you hitting 100% you die, no matter your grade or how much experience in the army you have.
During gunfights, even if you ambush them, under cover and the guy is on plain sight you STILL have to hit him a lot of times before elite enemies die. This is stupid. Normal grunts usually die in one hit, from silver and over its like they are bulletproof.
The second issue is the fact that cones of vision and hearing ranges are completely bonkers and they will screw you around. I can't stress enough how much this is important in this kind of game.
There is absolutely randomness on when it does happens. A patrol with a dog can ignore the corpse you left far from them and the fourth time they do the same route they find it, and you are far in the map cause you thought "ok that’s fine they will not find it”.
Also enemies can see trough a 20x20 window near the roof and spot a corpse you left on the floor. Height differences are completely ignored, even if you clearly see the cone of vision ignoring that zone.
Hearing is absolutely random, a corpse falling alert people over solid concrete walls on time, another time is ignored by the guy at 2m from them.
This stuff can't happen in those games. Playing on hard or without a finger on the quick save is impossible, there is too much uncertainty on how things works that makes this game a pain to play. You can be the best master planner in the universe, something will screw up.
In the end I kept playing but some missions are excruciatingly painful for this issue.
It’s not a bad game but needed more fixing and design competence.

I've played very few games which have earned the right to mention the Holocaust in their story. WW2 games are so often indulgent, desensitizing, gentrification of the most atrocious period of European history. Partisans 1941 is such a game that deals with its subject manner in a way that's tactful, honest, inglorious, and grim, thus following through on the seemingly insurmountable challenge of merely mentioning the Holocaust within the context of an action-entertainment product. 

If one gets invested in the story (not for everyone because it unfolds slowly within a very drab and solemn atmosphere), one finds that they grown sincerely dedicated to the tragic fate that the partisans find themselves in. You gain personal attachments to the characters; a little boy weilding a shotgun that's bigger than him, a busybody nurse who's compassion is a sacred blessing as well as lethal curse, a wandering assasin who's committed his life to satiating his bottomless thirst for bloody vengence, all these personalities and more become trusty companions, fulfilling unique roles and bearing unique and complex interpersonal burdons. This dark and haunting atmosphere is not for everyone. Some people will be put to sleep by it. As for myself, a huge history buff, this game scratches a kind of itch which most other WW2 games can't. 

The gameplay is truly engaging, immersive, and even hypnotic. When truly on a roll, the player may feel truly in touch witht that primal, hunting instinct. Looking at a map full of 80 nazis then, an hour later, seeing a graveyard full of 80 dead nazis, knowing that YOU made that happen with 3 Russians (one with a broken arm and having used around 200 rounds and a knife), you feel a sense of power that can't be accomplished through button mashing or spraying and praying. You have to get creative, take a breath and assess the situation, use your loot resourcefully, backtrack and try again, and otherwise engage in mentally engaging tactical executions. It isn't all just winding a clock though. Sometimes, timing things just right is what's needed to get out of a situation. 

That said, like sex, once things get going and the stealth gloves come off, that's when the real fun begins. The action is like nothing else. It is so damn exhilarating. Firefights may last only 1 minute or so. However, in that time frame, you're still required to make quick and decisive decisions. The character animations as they duck in cover, change stances to reload, and sprint across firing lanes heightens the stakes and offers a sight for the player to behold. This cycle of silence and caution which suddenly explodes into raw, unhinged fun violence is extremely rewarding. Even more rewarding when your play unfolds perfectly and you can just sit back and enjoy as the Nazis hit the floor. What looked like 15 nazis initially turning into 15 dead ones in 5 seconds as the smoke clears is like no feeling you can get from and RTS or sniper elite. 

That said, 
There is a massive issue with bugs in this game. It is severe. So severe that one may lose or need to restart missions simply due to bugs. Bugs are usually just annoyances, but in a STEALTH game that requires precision at its core is irredeemable and unacceptable. 

The game takes an EXTRAORDINARY amount of patience to play. Add bugs to that and you can imagine why this game will not appeal to 90%  of players.

As someone who's thoroughly enjoyed similar games to this (Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, and Desperados III), I picked this up during the summer sale expecting an awesome experience, especially since I enjoyed the demo of this game back before the full game was released. However, in practice, the game feels much less satisfying than similar titles, with an uninspiring and boring story.  

The first issue i have with the game is just how RANDOM it is. you only have a random chance to avoid hits when in cover, you have a random chance to hit enemies based on distance (you can even miss shots point blank if you're unlucky), you have a random chance to completely blow your cover when trying to stealth kill certain enemies if you don't have the skills for it. All of this randomness combined just made me feel like the only way I could properly complete a mission is if i save-scummed constantly. 

Second, not only is the story bland and uninteresting, but the characters are rather boring both in terms of personality and in terms of their skill sets. You simply throw them a gun they're a little bit better with and MAYBE they get a unique skill or two. As of the time I gave up on trying to enjoy this game, the only unique skills I had were the main character's throwing knife, and a child's abilities to disguise and to stun enemies with a slingshot (which was borderline useless, as you had to kill them before they woke up or your cover would be blown. Basically a worse throwing knife). Additionally, most missions I played forced me to stay completely undetected and/or never fire my weapons, which meant that the only way I could safely navigate the missions was by spamming the throwing knife and disguise abilities, while my third character sat there doing absolutely nothing the entire time as they were useless in terms of their skill set. What's the point of having so many weapon skills in the character's skill trees if you can't even use them most of the time? 

Overall, I would not recommend this game to anyone, as much better versions of this game exist already. 

TL;DR: Just play Shadow Tactics or Desperados III instead.

Already put in some good hours into the game so far and all in hard mode (no saves). Couple of things to say here:

Good things:

1) Decent story. Keeps me engaged and it's big chilling to see the campfire interactions after every mission. 
2) Fun combat, and devs did a good job in making gunfights a completely viable approach many situations. Assuming you don't attempt to shoot literally every enemy you see, you'll get enough ammo and explosives to play with. 

3) Cool skill system. Makes very noticeable impact in how you decide to play the game.

Bad things (and some are really really bad):

1) Overall character control is atrocious. In a world where Commandos, Desperados, and Shadow Tactics exist, there is absolutely no excuse for how bad and clunky character control is in this game. Things that I was taking for granted in the original Commandos, RELEASED IN 1998, are somehow broken in this game. Specifically:

a) If you issue a kill command with your knife (to include zorin's knife throw) and the enemy soldier moves, your character will just walk there, sit still, and get shot. In most cases any movement from the enemy will flat out cancel your command. Your characters don't like to follow the enemy for the kill for whatever reason. It's rage inducing at times as a player and it points toward laziness from the dev side. Like, come on guys, people were getting this right 15 years ago.

b) Game does not like it when you have multiple commands going out to different characters at the same time. Works in most cases, but happens enough to be noticeable.

c) Object placement's range is a random dice roll. All those games above will give you a range indicator of how far you can place that bottle of wine away from your character, for example. This game? none of that. And worse yet, it isn't consistent. You can place a bait bottle like 2 bodies out from the bush you're in one time and can't place it outside the bush the next. 

d) Your left click does waaaaaaaaay too much. You accidentally click on a body? You moving that sucker. It gets insanely obnoxious when  you're playing around tight spaces or small brushes when you're trying to both hide the bodies and your own character. other games would have you held down Ctrl or something to pick them up or to inspect inventory. Simple solution, but it makes the game smooth. Not only that, some genius had the idea of packing at least 2 huge selectable buttons when you mouse over the bodies. Like, which genius UI designer was it who thought that was a good idea?

2) Moving on from the controls, the stealth/hidden system isn't very clearly defined. It's not buggy (too much), but what you do to stay not detected or not (sometimes a specific criteria for finishing a mission) is not very clear cut. If, say, you use an infantry mine to blow up a patrolling squad with a dog, as long as no one saw the soldiers dying, enemy who can hear the explosion ran there to inspect, try to find you, and then walk away. IT DOESN'T break your stealth. But, if you gun down a lone guy in a random ass corner of the map and no one else is around? You're detected. If you kill someone with a knife, ran away to the other side of map, and then the body gets spotted? You're detected. On top of that, as others have pointed out before me, they're really good at running toward you, no matter where you are. If you run sufficiently far away they'll stop after a bit so it's not that bad though.

3) Game is bug infested. Characters got stuck in the middle of trees, pathing gets messed up, etc. You name it, they got it. I got a current bug right now where Zorin wouldn't fire his rifle after a mission. Went online to look for it, and lo and behold the error was mentioned A YEAR AND A HALF AGO. None of the fixes that worked then work now either. Devs somehow managed to patch the fixes out but not the bug. Brilliant.

That fact alone might be circumventable in most circumstances, but what doesnt help this at all is the additional issue of your not yet spotted guys to immediately open fire as soon as the spotting actually occurs, making it all the more difficult to really play this as a stealth tactics game when more often than not you just end up in a firefight halfway through anyways.

Characters all engage in combat immediately and are in constant agro until you take manual control and stop them. I kept my original review at the bottom because someone was upset that I reviewed the game with 8 hours played.  I felt like 8 hours was enough to have a reasonable opinion about the gameplay and mechanics, but I told them I'd finish the game and update my review anyway.

My opinions haven't really changed since my original review, and if anything, they further cement my problems with the game.

- Stealth is just too good in this game, and the lack of variety in stealth is what makes it get quickly stale.  What doesn't help at all is that the enemy AI is quite dumb and predictable. Every single enemy in the game does one of two things: stand in one spot and only look in one direction, or walk a route where they will inevitably look left, then straight, then right, and they may finally repeat that looking pattern a couple more times before moving elsewhere.  It doesn't really feel all that cool or rewarding, which is a shame because I'm a fan of stealth.  If you're hoping for something even remotely close or interesting to your favorite stealth games, this isn't it.

- The only thing I'll slightly change is that gunplay *can* feel decent if your character skills have weapon accuracy maxed and the weapon has an accuracy upgrade.  There's a few other things that can affect accuracy such as injuries, but until your weapon accuracy situation is in the best state it can possibly be in, it's just not that good.  It's worth mentioning that even when your weapon accuracy is the best it can be, it's still completely inferior to stealth.  There aren't many missions where stealth can't be used at all, either.

Additionally, here's some glitches and general frustrations I came across.  No spoilers ahead.

- One time when my partisan was downed, their body teleported across the map.

- Sanek's disguise ability makes it so you can't save the game because "the character is busy".  However, there was a time where after he was no longer disguised, the game insisted that he was still "busy".  I tried putting the disguise back on and then removing it again, but still the same issue.  My only way of fixing this was loading to an earlier save, which is frustrating.

- During one mission where you need to kill an important enemy, the important enemy runs off to a nearby village.  During one of my attempts, the important enemy started to casually walk in the middle of a firefight towards the area he just ran away from.  This is not expected behavior, as he's supposed to stand until we engage in a cutscene with him.

- If you're in the enemy cone of vision, they start to get suspicious (which is expected).  You can do just about any action without immediately alarming them while in their vision.  You can throw a grenade, throw a rock, heal yourself, and it's no issue.  You know what is an issue?  Placing a harmless bottle on the ground.  Placing a bottle on the ground in their cone of vision IMMEDIATELY alerts all nearby enemies.  Let me emphasize that you can throw a grenade in their vision, but not place a harmless bottle.

- Mission failed screen has been completely unresponsive a few times, causing me to quit the game completely to fix it.

- I've had partisan #1 stuck in the reviving animation if they happen to get downed while reviving partisan #2.  This also caused the partisan #2 to be 100% incapable of being revived (which is never supposed to happen).  Additionally, if you revive partisan #1, they will be perpetually in that same reviving animation, and totally unable to commit any actions other than gliding across the ground.  Had to load a different save to fix this.

- You can actually throw grenades over the walls of an adjacent room, even though the walls clearly go all the way up to the ceiling.  May take a few tries to get the height and angle right, also assuming the wall isn't too high.  One particularly egregious example of this is killing the final important enemy in the final mission.

- One mission has you running away from a ton of soldiers who are actively trying to find you.  Once you get to the exit, a cutscene plays.  However, I started to hear gunfire unrelated to the cutscene.  I quickly realized that the cutscene is just playing over the mission I was just in, and my partisans were not teleported to a safe location.  They were actually fighting even though I reached the exit.  My partisans died, and I saw a "mission failed" screen while the cutscene was still playing.  Moments later, I saw a "mission successful" screen placed over top of the "mission failed" screen, which is all still placed over the cutscene.  This is confusing, annoying, and inexcusable.

- There are a few other glitches or annoying things, but the ones above were particularly annoying.

I do have a few nice things to say about the game.

- Voice acting was pretty okay.

- Between story missions, you can assign partisans to do some base missions for gathering resources.  This is a nice extra touch to the game, though it definitely could have been fleshed out more.

Overall, I still cannot recommend this game.  Most of the game felt okay, but the actual gameplay is where it truly fell short.  It felt boring, unrewarding, and more of a chore than anything.


===ORIGINAL REVIEW===
I wanted to like this game so much, but the combat is so bad.  

Stealth is king in this game, but enemy routes are the same 100% of the time.  This makes for somewhat bland and not-so-creative gameplay.  Stealth really just consists of sneaking up behind an enemy, knifing them, and then hiding their body.  Seems fairly simple (and it is), but it gets really repetitive.  To be honest, stealth is likely too good, and in stark contrast to awful gunplay.  What's really annoying is that if you're caught, all nearby enemies suddenly know your position on the map, no matter what.  Really bizarre oversight and frustrating to experience.  

Gunplay feels so bad.  After the first few missions, enemy soldiers tend to have great accuracy while your accuracy is still mediocre.  You can use cover to make enemy accuracy go down a bit, but it ultimately feels like you're always at a disadvantage.  You could argue that you're going against trained soldiers, but the repetitive stealth is just not that fun to make up for that.  You can upgrade your accuracy for certain guns and other skills, which can help a bit, but not enough in my experience.

For anyone claiming this is like XCOM or Fallout, that is a completely mistaken comparison.  Combat is real-time in this game, whereas that isn't the case with XCOM and classic Fallout games.  Combat becomes far too chaotic if you're not prepared for it, and your squad will likely die unless you had intentionally engaged in a gun fight.  If you think you can quickly micro-manage your squad in the middle of a gunfight like an RTS game, it's really not that effective.

The story is otherwise alright and the aesthetics are cool, but the gameplay is just not there for me.  I've tried coming back to this game a couple of times now, but I just can't get myself to enjoy this game.

Partisans 1941 is a well designed real-time tactics game with a great historical flavour. Although you have a wide variety of ways to distract, ambush, and assassinate enemies, the missions are quite challenging and will have you looking at multiple ways to achieve your objective. These tough missions are ingeniously interspersed with relaxing 'camp building' segments where you can help your fledgling partisan group flourish by repairing and upgrading weapons, managing inventory, and sending them on morale-building side missions.

Not great, but a solid game. The AI and the engine is only slightly worse then the one of games like Shadow Tactics (for example a platform of half a meter height blocks sight cones of enemy soldiers, even when they are on the higher ground), the graphics are decent, the occasional firefights are not bad.

What I see as the worst part of the game is probably the story. Basically it's about killing Nazis, which is always good, but here it's a LOT of Soviet/Russian pathos and propaganda, especially in today's light of things happening on Ukraine: All the partisans are strong and intelligent people, all looks like fashion models, most talks about how successful they were in study or sport - clearly trying to picture that only the best of the best became partisans. All the characters are completely shallow and flawless. And anything of Soviet making is presented as a great and righteous, including highly controversial stuff like Finnish Winter War. You can look on this like that's all a comic book hyperbole, like a comics with Captain America (then you will be fine), or you can feel that the authors meant of all this for real (and then you can be slightly disgusted).

Really liked the game and played trough the main story and the DLC. Graphics sound and the whole game atmosphere is pretty solid. Took some time to figure out things but at the end used my squad pretty effectively. I guess you first need to figure out your style, catching enemies in an ambush or slowly thinning the heard. For me was the former, on some missions really took the time to to get them all.
Same goes for the meta game (between the missions), took some time to get used to but IMHO the game could do without it.
The game had a few downsides as well, performance wasn't great and it felt laggy a lot (well until you get used to it) and occasionally the units didn't really do what I had in mind (eg. doing a mele instead of a knife trow). Still if you like real-time tactics I suggest you go and give it a go.

At the end of the mission I have to send a signal to the Soviet air force to bomb the place to smithereens, [b]AND THE MOMENT I DO THIS[/b] the whole hell breaks loose. Every single soldier on the map starts looking for me, and the game sends me wave after wave of infinite heavy reinforcements. So I do the sensible thing, I do what the game asked me to do and [b]GTFO[/b]. But guess what? Does the game let me [b]GTFO? NOPE.[/b] I arrive at the extraction point and nothing happens, at which point I am stupefied. Am I doing something wrong? Or did the game break again? If I am doing something wrong, then what the hell am I doing wrong? As the game just tells me to leave. So I figure, perhaps the game won't let me leave because there's enemies around... [b]WHY?![/b] I can easily dodge them and get the hell out of there. But nope. At this point I cheese the game, I place a bunch of traps and mines at the point in which the reinforcements just appear out of nowhere. I have Sanek, the kid to trigger the event and get to me as fast as he can, as he's the nimblest of the group. Despite all odds, this somehow works out... without a prompt to leave which I saw in a playthrough (let me guess, another damn bug?).

That one mission just tells everything you need to know about the game. A horribly buggy game with atrocious game design. The level lets you do it in one way and one way alone. You can't even fit through train carts that anyone could fit through, you gotta take a U-turn on a heavily guarded checkpoint [b]FOR SOME DARN REASON.[/b] You can't even scale a meter high obstacle of any kind. And then all of a sudden the mission that would punish you with game over for failing stealth, turns into a Michael Bay movie... What is this schizo game design? Who thought this was a good idea? And yes, of course it has to have mandatory stealth missions that are the absolute worst part, which only complements the disgustingly buggy mess that this game is. And the dogs... don't even get me started on the dogs. Sometimes they smell you through a foot of concrete, sometimes they can't even sense you being a meter away, and other times they spot you across the damn map, and start running around like complete spastics (I noticed that on a single level with multiple floors), jeopardizing your one shot stealth mission. And god forbid if the enemies spot a corpse while you're half-way across the level which nets you an automatic game over. And of course every damn nazi in the world knows what you're up to the moment you're spotted, that goes without saying.

Don't get me wrong. When the game works, it works really, really well. It's at its best when it doesn't hold your hand and lets you experiment with tactics. There's nothing more satisfying than killing a couple dozen nazis in a well executed ambush. But that's only a small part of the game that the developers didn't choose to capitalize on. Instead for every good mission you get a mandatory stealth mission, and for every single mission in equal part you get mundane busy work such as sending your comrades to fish or to chop wood. Like I get what they were going for with the latter, a partisan's life is mostly about just trying to survive in the wilderness. I get it, but it doesn't make it any less boring.

The base management just in general is half-baked at best. You can build a number of auxiliary buildings such as a workshop, a hunting tower, a chicken den, a medical tent, and a lumber yard. The workshop is only marginally useful for upgrades, but I never once crafted one of the 4 (!) items it lets me craft, as I was getting enough stuff from missions and between mission ambushes. Again, Partisans has weapon rarity (why?), so what ends up happening is you just keep delaying upgrading weapons until you find the golden best. The hunting tower is just completely useless as I would get triple as much food from chickens and fishing. As for lumber, it's useful at first, but by the end I had 1500 units of it, not knowing what to do with. Same goes with the skills, some of them are either useless, or are just bugged out, like the human shield and the slingshot. I mostly just used Zorin's throwing knives and Fetisov's bullet storm. Morozov is also useful during stealth only missions. as he's the best at it.

The characters are really just kinda boring in general too. You get a number of archetypes in here: a stoic soldier, a larger than life old man, a medically inclined female, a determined kid, a thief with a heart of gold. The most unusual apple here is an NKVD officer who is pragmatic, but is also very much humanized, unlike in all of the клюква that we're used to by now. He's pretty useless in a fight, so I just let him fish however. And if you think that's anticlimactic, then so is the ending that is as abrupt as the many invisible walls in the game (in the year 2020!).

I understand the effort on display, but I simply cannot recommend it. If everything that I've said so far doesn't convince you, then there's the final nail in the coffin. Commandos style real time strategy game focused around a Russian resistance group in 1941. A larger focus on being able to engage in direct combat than most games like this, as stealth or avoiding kills is rarely required, weapons of different qualities can be found and upgraded as well as traps and grenades. Characters gain experience from kills, objectives completed, and side missions you assign them at your camp between stages and can learn new abilities, passive skills, or increase their hit chance with weapons. Between missions you have a camp where you can assign characters tasks like missions to get them XP or to gain equipment, tasks to gain food or resources, building mines or grenades, etc. A lot of elements never amount to much, your morale should always be at max so that's never a thing that matters, getting food is never really a problem, upgrading weapons and crafting explosives feels like an afterthought, all the looting is just time consuming.

Bigger problems with the game are that Desperados 3 added the thing most needed in this genre, a fast forward button, and that's always going to be missed. Unbalanced, enemies are never set up in a difficult way that really requires you to use skills of multiple characters, some very overpowered abilities. Not a great idea to go for achievements requiring stealth as what actually counts as detection can be buggy and completing main objectives can just alert anymore for no reason. It doesn't know how to handle height or cover when it comes to your enemies cones of view and having no difference between things that are standing, crouching, or on the ground is unfortunate. If you go for a more combat focused playthrough one of the biggest bugs is that they just won't reload guns and if you manually do it they go through the animation but nothing happens (opening inventory and unequipping and reequipping seems to get it working again). You can go into a time slowed mode where you can issue commands to all your characters to try to sync up actions but you really can't do things like have them move in together to each stealth kill an enemy as your window between an alert going off is probably around one second and it is one of the kind of games where it doesn't matter if an enemy is able to say/yell/radio/etc a warning because the alert comes the second they see anything (even if that something is the knife flying through the air to kill them).

If you really like the genre there is some enjoyment to be had and I can recommend it but it falls a bit short in many areas always staying around just being an average title at best.

TLDR
Partisans is a spiritual clone of Commandos with elements of Shadow Tactics and some base building and character progression elements. At its core it is 2.5D tactical real time strategy with an emphasis on stealth where you generally control 3 partisans per mission. Sure, you can equip your partisans with weapons and even upgrade them, set up choke points and traps for Nazi patrols, but stealth is just much more efficient. The actual gunfire engagements do feel unbalanced and quite buggy where AI won’t react to a landmine going of with a loud bang if they are 20+ meters away.
From the stealth mechanics point of view the game does encourage planning and combining of your squad skills. Occasional bugs and glitches do affect the game, but all in all will not prevent you from enjoying the game. The challenges that the maps present are not huge though, planning, timing and having your best team on the map will make it easy with only occasional need for quickloads.
The story is non-existent – for motherland and for Stalin, let’s kill as many Nazis as we can and sabotage them. Occasional campfire discussions are aimed to create an authentic atmosphere, but they are so badly done that I rather not have them at all. Historical notes on the other had (you recover these during missions) do give you some glimpses of the war on the Soviet front.
Base-building is redundant, it is there to pass some time and also give you an option to upgrade weapons and manage your inventory, but otherwise it is so easy that I did not even notice any challenges with food and supply management (you loot enough during campaign missions and basebuilding auto missions).
In overall the game is solid, it has its flaws and is certainly few steps behind Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3, but otherwise it is worth your wile if you are a fan of the genre, and common, ‘killing Nazis is always fun’ as per William "B.J." Blazkowicz.
